chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Muhammad ibn Ismail, from al-Himyari, from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qummi, who said:

Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said: 'The one who performs Ziyarah of the grave of my father in Baghdad is like the one who performed Ziyarah of the grave of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), except that for the Messenger of Allah and for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them both) is their distinct merit.'

key_terms.أَمِيرِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Imam Ali AS)
key_terms.قَبْرَ أَبِي: grave of my father (referring to Imam Musa al-Kazim)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of visiting Imam Musa al-Kazim's grave in Baghdad compared to the Prophet and Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) equates the reward of visiting Imam Musa al-Kazim’s grave in Baghdad with that of the Prophet and Imam Ali, highlighting the elevated status of the Imams as successors to prophetic authority. The distinction made by the phrase 'except for their specific merit' (illa anna la-rasulillahi wa li-amir al-mu'minin fadl-huma) clarifies that while the spiritual reward is comparable, the intrinsic rank of the Prophet and the Commander of the Faithful remains uniquely superior, a nuance often discussed in Shia exegetical traditions regarding the hierarchy of the Ahl al-Bayt.
